claim: In Gravesend a door that opens by hand gets no lever beside it; a lever opens something that cannot be opened by hand (the owner's ruling on its shop doors). The campaign's lever is tile 1070: 283 sprites over the 43 maps, 184 of them wall-aligned, the 156 pushed ones in switches-v1.json mounted at a median 0.785 player heights; 280 carry a tx, the modal command is 1 (kCmdOn, 147), and 160 set trigger_push and 241 trigger_on.
evidence: the owner, 2026-11-25: 'some of the shops have lever next to it, but it just opens door the same way you would interact with them' (projects/blood-city/level/l3_theatre.py:369-370)
knowledge/blood/findings/probes/audit2_lever_1070.py over the 43 campaign maps (every sprite of tile 1070): 283, 184 wall-aligned, 280 with tx, command 1 on 147, trigger_push 160, trigger_on 241
knowledge/blood/design/switches-v1.json rows with picnum 1070 and how 'pushed': 156, median above_floor_humans 0.785 (by_how.pushed, 0.79, is of every pushed switch tile)
use: Place levers through bloodmap.switches.pressed_switch, which sets trigger_push and trigger_on; a hand-rolled one could not be pushed. Say on and off when it is to work both ways.
